```odin
import midi "fire:midi"
```

MIDI 1.0 messages, their Universal MIDI Packet (UMP) encoding, and helpers.
Drivers speak UMP (CoreMIDI, Windows MIDI Services) or bytes (ALSA, WinMM);
the engine works with MIDI 1.0 bytes. See /design/backend/.

## Constants

### MAX_PORTS

```odin
MAX_PORTS :: 16
```

Number of input port indices: ports are tagged 0 ..< MAX_PORTS.

### UMP_SYSTEM

```odin
UMP_SYSTEM :: 0x1
```

UMP message type (top 4 bits of the first word): system real-time and common.

### UMP_MIDI1_VOICE

```odin
UMP_MIDI1_VOICE :: 0x2
```

UMP message type: MIDI 1.0 channel voice.

### UMP_DATA64

```odin
UMP_DATA64 :: 0x3
```

UMP message type: 64-bit data, which carries 7-bit SysEx.

## Types

### Port_Direction

```odin
Port_Direction :: enum u8 {
	Input,
	Output,
}
```

Whether a port is a source (we receive from it) or a destination (we send
to it).

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Input` | a source we can receive from |
| `Output` | a destination we can send to |

### Port_Info

```odin
Port_Info :: struct {
	id: string,
	name: string,
	direction: Port_Direction,
}
```

One port as listed by `enumerate`. Pass `id` to `open_input` or
`open_output`. The strings are owned by the slice; free the whole slice
with `port_infos_destroy`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | stable across runs where the OS allows it |
| `name` | display name |
| `direction` | .Input = source, .Output = destination |

### Port

```odin
Port :: u32
```

Handle to an open port. 0 is invalid.

### Driver_VTable

```odin
Driver_VTable :: struct {
	destroy: proc(d: ^Driver),
	enumerate: proc(d: ^Driver, allocator: mem.Allocator) -> ([]Port_Info, core.Error),
	open_input: proc(d: ^Driver, id: string, port_index: u8) -> (Port, core.Error),
	open_output: proc(d: ^Driver, id: string) -> (Port, core.Error),
	create_virtual_input: proc(d: ^Driver, name: string, port_index: u8) -> (Port, core.Error),
	create_virtual_output: proc(d: ^Driver, name: string) -> (Port, core.Error),
	close: proc(d: ^Driver, port: Port),
	send: proc(d: ^Driver, port: Port, message: []u8, time_ns: u64) -> core.Error,
}
```

A MIDI driver wraps one OS API. All procs run on the control thread, except
`send`, which runs on the Midi_Output sender thread (or the control thread).
Input from every open input port goes to `Driver.input`, tagged with the
port index given at open.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `destroy` |  |
| `enumerate` |  |
| `open_input` |  |
| `open_output` |  |
| `create_virtual_input` | A destination other apps can send to; its input arrives on `port_index`. |
| `create_virtual_output` | A source other apps can receive from; send to it like an output. |
| `close` |  |
| `send` | One complete message: a short message, or F0 … F7. `time_ns` on the host clock; 0 = now. Drivers that can schedule (CoreMIDI) do. |

### Driver

```odin
Driver :: struct {
	vtable: ^Driver_VTable,
	name: string,
	data: rawptr,
	input: ^Midi_Input,
	can_schedule: bool,
	event_lock: sync.Mutex,
	events: [64]Event,
	event_head: int,
	event_count: int,
	events_dropped: int,
}
```

One OS MIDI API, created by a driver package (`fire:midi/coremidi`,
`fire:midi/alsa`, `fire:midi/winmm`) and freed with `driver_destroy`. Set
`input` before opening input ports. Read hot-plug events with `poll_event`.
The event fields are internal to `poll_event` and `driver_notify`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `vtable` | the driver's implementation |
| `name` | API name, e.g. "CoreMIDI" |
| `data` | the driver's own state |
| `input` | set before opening inputs |
| `can_schedule` | The OS delivers a timestamped send at its time (CoreMIDI, ALSA). If false (WinMM), Midi_Output's sender thread holds messages until then. |
| `event_lock` | Driver notification threads → control thread (see poll_event). |
| `events` |  |
| `event_head` |  |
| `event_count` |  |
| `events_dropped` |  |

### Event_Kind

```odin
Event_Kind :: enum u8 {
	Ports_Changed,
	Port_Lost,
}
```

What a driver `Event` reports.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Ports_Changed` | ports appeared or disappeared: re-enumerate |
| `Port_Lost` | an open port's device went away; `port` says which. Close it. |

### Event

```odin
Event :: struct {
	kind: Event_Kind,
	port: Port,
}
```

A hot-plug event, read with `poll_event`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `kind` |  |
| `port` | the lost port (Port_Lost only) |

### Input_Event

```odin
Input_Event :: struct {
	time_ns: u64,
	port: u8,
	bytes: [3]u8,
}
```

One short message received by a driver, on its way to the audio thread.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `time_ns` | host clock (rt.host_time_ns) |
| `port` | port index given at open |
| `bytes` | MIDI 1.0 message; unused bytes are 0 |

### Midi_Input

```odin
Midi_Input :: struct {
	queue: Spsc_Queue($T=Input_Event),
	producer_lock: sync.Mutex,
	sysex: Sysex_Queue,
	assemblers: [16]Sysex_Assembler,
	parsers: [16]Byte_Parser,
	sysex_storage: []u8,
	latency_ns: u64,
	pending: []Input_Event,
	pending_len: int,
	late: u64,
	dropped: u64,
	ignored: u64,
}
```

Collects MIDI input from driver threads and places it, sample-accurately,
into audio blocks.

Timing: an event received at host time t is played at t + latency_ns. With
latency ≥ (output_ns − callback_ns) + one driver period, every event arrives
before its block is rendered, so timing is jitter-free at a fixed latency.
Use `suggested_latency_ns`. Events that arrive too late for their slot are
placed at offset 0 and counted in `late`.

Set up with `input_init`, free with `input_destroy`. Read SysEx from
`sysex` with `sysex_pop` (control thread) and counters with `input_stats`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `queue` | driver threads → audio thread |
| `producer_lock` | driver threads; never taken by the audio thread |
| `sysex` | complete SysEx for the control thread (sysex_pop) |
| `assemblers` | per-port SysEx reassembly |
| `parsers` | for drivers that deliver MIDI 1.0 bytes |
| `sysex_storage` | backing memory for the assemblers |
| `latency_ns` | atomic; see input_set_latency |
| `pending` | Audio thread only. sorted by time |
| `pending_len` | events in use at the start of pending |
| `late` | Counters (atomic). events placed at offset 0 because they arrived too late |
| `dropped` | short messages lost to a full queue or pending buffer |
| `ignored` | UMP messages with no MIDI 1.0 meaning (MIDI 2.0 voice, utility...) |

### Input_Config

```odin
Input_Config :: struct {
	queue_capacity: int,
	pending_capacity: int,
	sysex_bytes: int,
	sysex_messages: int,
	max_sysex_len: int,
}
```

Sizes for `input_init`. A zero config means `default_input_config()`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `queue_capacity` | short messages in flight |
| `pending_capacity` | messages waiting for a future block |
| `sysex_bytes` | SysEx byte ring to the control thread |
| `sysex_messages` | SysEx messages in flight to the control thread |
| `max_sysex_len` | bytes per port; longer SysEx messages are dropped |

### Byte_Parser

```odin
Byte_Parser :: struct {
	status: u8,
	data: [2]u8,
	have: int,
	need: int,
	in_sysex: bool,
}
```

Running-status state for one byte-stream source. SysEx bytes go to the
port's Sysex_Assembler buffer.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `status` | current running status (0 = none) |
| `data` |  |
| `have` |  |
| `need` |  |
| `in_sysex` |  |

### Input_Stats

```odin
Input_Stats :: struct {
	late: u64,
	dropped: u64,
	ignored: u64,
	sysex_dropped: u64,
}
```

Counters since `input_init`, read with `input_stats`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `late` | events placed at offset 0 because they arrived too late |
| `dropped` | short messages lost to a full queue or pending buffer |
| `ignored` | messages with no MIDI 1.0 meaning, stray data bytes |
| `sysex_dropped` | SysEx too long, malformed, or lost to a full queue |

### Output_Event

```odin
Output_Event :: struct {
	time_ns: u64,
	port: Port,
	bytes: [3]u8,
}
```

One short message for `output_push`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `time_ns` | host clock; when the message should leave the port |
| `port` | an output or virtual output of the Midi_Output's driver |
| `bytes` | MIDI 1.0 short message; unused bytes are ignored |

### Midi_Output

```odin
Midi_Output :: struct {
	driver: ^Driver,
	queue: Spsc_Queue($T=Output_Event),
	thread: ^thread.Thread,
	running: bool,
	dropped: u64,
	errors: u64,
	sent: u64,
}
```

Short messages from the audio thread to the OS. The audio thread pushes
timestamped events; a sender thread hands them to the driver, which
schedules them (CoreMIDI) or sends them at once. Timestamps should lead the
wall clock by at least the output latency, so sending is never late.

Set up with `output_init`, then `output_start`; free with `output_destroy`.
The counters may be read atomically from any thread.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `driver` | driver the sender thread sends through |
| `queue` | audio thread → sender thread |
| `thread` | sender thread; nil when stopped |
| `running` | atomic |
| `dropped` | atomic: queue full |
| `errors` | atomic: driver send failed |
| `sent` | atomic |

### Sysex_Queue

```odin
Sysex_Queue :: struct {...}
```

Complete SysEx messages from driver threads to the control thread. One
producer at a time (Midi_Input serializes its drivers) and one consumer.
Payloads (without F0/F7) live in a byte ring; descriptors in an SPSC queue.
Fields are internal.

### Sysex_Message

```odin
Sysex_Message :: struct {
	time_ns: u64,
	port: u8,
	data: []u8,
}
```

One complete SysEx message, returned by `sysex_pop`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `time_ns` | host clock time of arrival (of the final byte) |
| `port` | port index given at open |
| `data` | payload without F0/F7; owned by the caller of sysex_pop |

### Sysex_Status

```odin
Sysex_Status :: enum u8 {
	Complete = 0,
	Start = 1,
	Continue = 2,
	End = 3,
}
```

Status field of a UMP SysEx (data64) packet.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Complete` | the whole message in one packet |
| `Start` | first packet of several |
| `Continue` | a middle packet |
| `End` | last packet |

### Sysex_Assembler

```odin
Sysex_Assembler :: struct {
	buffer: []u8,
	len: int,
	active: bool,
	overflowed: bool,
}
```

Reassembles SysEx from UMP data64 packets for one source. The buffer is
preallocated; a message longer than it is dropped (and counted).

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `buffer` | caller-provided storage; its length is the maximum message size |
| `len` | payload bytes so far |
| `active` | inside a message |
| `overflowed` | the current message did not fit |

### Sysex_Result

```odin
Sysex_Result :: enum u8 {
	None,
	Complete,
	Dropped,
}
```

What `sysex_assemble` did with a packet.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `None` | more packets needed (or nothing to do) |
| `Complete` | `assembler_message` holds a complete payload |
| `Dropped` | message too long or malformed; discarded |

## Procedures

### port_infos_destroy

```odin
port_infos_destroy :: proc(infos: []Port_Info, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Frees a slice returned by `enumerate`, including its strings. Pass the same
allocator that was given to `enumerate`.

### poll_event

```odin
poll_event :: proc(d: ^Driver) -> (e: Event, ok: bool)
```

Control thread. Hot-plug events in the order the driver saw them.

### driver_notify

```odin
driver_notify :: proc "contextless"(d: ^Driver, e: Event)
```

Drivers call this from their notification thread (never an audio thread).
Consecutive Ports_Changed events are merged.

### driver_destroy

```odin
driver_destroy :: proc(d: ^Driver)
```

Control thread. Closes every open port and frees the driver. Nil is allowed.
Stop any Midi_Output using the driver first.

### enumerate

```odin
enumerate :: proc(d: ^Driver, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> ([]Port_Info, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Lists the sources and destinations the OS currently has.
The caller owns the result; free it with `port_infos_destroy`.

### open_input

```odin
open_input :: proc(d: ^Driver, id: string, port_index: u8) -> (Port, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Starts receiving from the source with this `id` (from
`enumerate`) into `Driver.input`, tagged with `port_index` (0 ..< MAX_PORTS).
Returns .Invalid_Argument if `input` is unset, the index is out of range or
the port is not found. Close the port with `close_port`.

### open_output

```odin
open_output :: proc(d: ^Driver, id: string) -> (Port, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Opens the destination with this `id` (from `enumerate`) for
`send`. Returns .Invalid_Argument if the port is not found. Close it with
`close_port`.

### create_virtual_input

```odin
create_virtual_input :: proc(d: ^Driver, name: string, port_index: u8) -> (Port, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Creates a destination called `name` that other apps can
send to; what they send arrives on `Driver.input` tagged with `port_index`.
Returns .Invalid_Argument as for `open_input`, or .Unsupported (WinMM).

### create_virtual_output

```odin
create_virtual_output :: proc(d: ^Driver, name: string) -> (Port, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Creates a source called `name` that other apps can receive
from. Send to it like an output. Returns .Unsupported on WinMM.

### close_port

```odin
close_port :: proc(d: ^Driver, port: Port)
```

Control thread. Closes a port opened or created on this driver. Unknown
handles are ignored.

### send

```odin
send :: proc(d: ^Driver, port: Port, message: []u8, time_ns: u64 = 0) -> core.Error
```

Sends one complete message: a short message or SysEx (F0 … F7). `time_ns` is
on the host clock (rt.host_time_ns); 0 sends now. Drivers that can schedule
send it at that time, others send at once. May block (WinMM SysEx); call it
from the control thread or the Midi_Output sender thread, never the audio
thread. Returns .Invalid_Argument for an empty or invalid message or a port
that is not an output.

### default_input_config

```odin
default_input_config :: proc() -> Input_Config
```

Queue and pending capacity 4096, a 64 KiB SysEx ring holding up to 256
messages, and 8 KiB per SysEx message.

### input_init

```odin
input_init :: proc(in_: ^Midi_Input, cfg: Input_Config = Input_Config{}, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (err: runtime.Allocator_Error)
```

Control thread. Allocates the queues and buffers; a zero `cfg` uses
`default_input_config()`. Free with `input_destroy` and the same allocator.

### input_destroy

```odin
input_destroy :: proc(in_: ^Midi_Input, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `input_init` allocated. Close every input port
that delivers to it and stop calling `input_process` first.

### suggested_latency_ns

```odin
suggested_latency_ns :: proc "contextless"(output_offset_ns: u64, buffer_frames: int, sample_rate: f64) -> u64
```

Latency that makes input timing jitter-free: the gap between a callback and
the presentation of its first frame, plus one driver period.

### input_set_latency

```odin
input_set_latency :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input, latency_ns: u64)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Sets the delay, in nanoseconds, between an event's arrival time and the
time it is placed in a block. Any thread; takes effect on the next block.

### input_push_short

```odin
input_push_short :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input, time_ns: u64, port: u8, bytes: [3]u8)
```

Driver threads. Queues one short message received at host time `time_ns` on
port index `port`. Never call it from the audio thread (it takes a mutex).
A full queue counts a drop.

### input_push_ump

```odin
input_push_ump :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input, time_ns: u64, port: u8, words: []u32)
```

Decodes a run of UMP words (MIDI 1.0 protocol). SysEx goes to the SysEx queue.

### input_push_bytes

```odin
input_push_bytes :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input, time_ns: u64, port: u8, bytes: []u8)
```

Parses a MIDI 1.0 byte stream (as from ALSA rawmidi/sequencer decoding or
WinMM): running status, real-time bytes anywhere (even inside other
messages), SysEx split across calls. Complete SysEx goes to the SysEx queue.

### input_process

```odin
input_process :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input, block_ns: u64, frames: int, sample_rate: f64, out: ^core.Event_Writer)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Writes the MIDI events due in this block to `out` as core.Midi_Raw, in
time order. `block_ns` is the presentation time of the block's first frame
(Io_Block.output_ns).

### input_drain

```odin
input_drain :: proc(in_: ^Midi_Input, each: proc(user: rawptr, port: u8, bytes: [3]u8, time_ns: u64), user: rawptr)
```

The consumer of a `Midi_Input` that isn't an audio thread: every short
message received so far, in time order, to `each` (with its port index
and bytes), with no latency or block placement. For control-thread uses
such as control surfaces: give such ports a `Midi_Input` of their own,
on a driver of their own, and drain it from one thread only. SysEx comes
from `sysex_pop` as usual.

### input_stats

```odin
input_stats :: proc "contextless"(in_: ^Midi_Input) -> Input_Stats
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Any thread. A snapshot of the input's counters.

### output_init

```odin
output_init :: proc(o: ^Midi_Output, d: ^Driver, capacity: int = 4096, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> runtime.Allocator_Error
```

Control thread. Allocates a queue of `capacity` events for sending through
driver `d`. Does not start the sender thread (see `output_start`).

### output_destroy

```odin
output_destroy :: proc(o: ^Midi_Output, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Stops the sender (sending what is queued) and frees the
queue. Use the allocator given to `output_init`.

### output_start

```odin
output_start :: proc(o: ^Midi_Output)
```

Control thread. Starts the high-priority sender thread. Does nothing if it
is already running.

### output_stop

```odin
output_stop :: proc(o: ^Midi_Output)
```

Control thread. Sends whatever is still queued, then joins the thread.

### output_push

```odin
output_push :: proc "contextless"(o: ^Midi_Output, e: Output_Event) -> bool
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Audio thread. Returns false (and counts a drop) when the queue is full.

### output_push_events

```odin
output_push_events :: proc "contextless"(o: ^Midi_Output, events: []core.Event, ports: []Port, block_ns: u64, sample_rate: f64) -> (pushed: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Pushes the `core.Midi_Raw` events among `events` (offsets into a
block presented at `block_ns`) to `o`, each to `ports[raw.port]`. Other
event kinds, and port indexes outside `ports`, are skipped. Returns how
many were queued. Use it to send a graph's MIDI output:

```odin
midi.output_push_events(&out, core.event_writer_events(&writer), ports[:], block.output_ns, sample_rate)
```

### frame_time_ns

```odin
frame_time_ns :: proc "contextless"(block_ns: u64, offset: int, sample_rate: f64) -> u64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Time of frame `offset` in a block presented at `block_ns`.

### sysex_queue_init

```odin
sysex_queue_init :: proc(q: ^Sysex_Queue, byte_capacity: int, message_capacity: int, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> runtime.Allocator_Error
```

Control thread. Allocates a byte ring of at least `byte_capacity` bytes
(rounded up to a power of two) and room for `message_capacity` messages.
Free with `sysex_queue_destroy` and the same allocator.

### sysex_queue_destroy

```odin
sysex_queue_destroy :: proc(q: ^Sysex_Queue, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Control thread. Frees what `sysex_queue_init` allocated.

### sysex_push

```odin
sysex_push :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Sysex_Queue, time_ns: u64, port: u8, payload: []u8) -> bool
```

Producer (driver thread). No allocation. Returns false (and counts a drop)
when full.

### sysex_pop

```odin
sysex_pop :: proc(q: ^Sysex_Queue, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (msg: Sysex_Message, ok: bool)
```

Consumer (control thread). Returns the oldest message; its `data` is
allocated with `allocator` and owned by the caller. ok = false when the queue
is empty (or the allocation failed, which discards the message).

### sysex_dropped

```odin
sysex_dropped :: proc "contextless"(q: ^Sysex_Queue) -> u64
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Any thread. Messages dropped so far: too long, malformed, or lost to a
full queue.

### message_length

```odin
message_length :: proc "contextless"(status: u8) -> int
```

Length in bytes of a MIDI 1.0 message with this status byte (0 = not a
complete short message on its own: data byte, SysEx start/end, undefined).

### ump_word_count

```odin
ump_word_count :: proc "contextless"(first_word: u32) -> int
```

UMP message type → words per packet (UMP spec 1.1, table 4).

### ump_from_short

```odin
ump_from_short :: proc "contextless"(bytes: [3]u8, group: u8 = 0) -> (word: u32, ok: bool)
```

Encodes a MIDI 1.0 short message as one UMP word. ok = false for SysEx or
invalid status bytes.

### ump_to_short

```odin
ump_to_short :: proc "contextless"(word: u32) -> (bytes: [3]u8, ok: bool)
```

Decodes a type 1 or type 2 UMP word into MIDI 1.0 bytes.

### ump_sysex_packet_count

```odin
ump_sysex_packet_count :: proc "contextless"(payload_len: int) -> int
```

Number of 2-word packets needed for a SysEx payload (without F0/F7).

### ump_sysex_packet

```odin
ump_sysex_packet :: proc "contextless"(payload: []u8, i: int, group: u8 = 0) -> [2]u32
```

Encodes one SysEx packet (index `i` of the payload) into two UMP words.

### sysex_assemble

```odin
sysex_assemble :: proc "contextless"(a: ^Sysex_Assembler, words: [2]u32) -> Sysex_Result
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread).-safe: no allocation. `words` is one data64 packet.

### assembler_message

```odin
assembler_message :: proc "contextless"(a: ^Sysex_Assembler) -> []u8
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). The payload assembled so far: after a .Complete result, the whole
message (without F0/F7). It aliases the assembler's buffer, so copy it
before the next packet.
